preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, call the lock() function with a time parameter (e.g., 1 second) to temporarily set ownership to address(0). This will disable all onlyOwner functions including fee adjustments, max transaction limits, and swap/liquidity features. Alternatively, call renounceOwnership() to permanently give up ownership. This disrupts contract management and can lead to frozen functionality.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract has a lock() function in the Ownable parent contract that allows the owner to temporarily set ownership to address(0). This disables all onlyOwner functions including fee adjustments, max transaction limits, and swap/liquidity features. The vulnerability allows an attacker (who becomes owner) to lock the contract, making it unmanageable.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Become the contract owner by overwriting the storage slot for _owner. 2. Call lock(1) to temporarily set owner to address(0). 3. Verify owner is now address(0).
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.store() to write attacker address to the _owner storage slot (slot 0). 2. Impersonate as attacker (now owner). 3. Call lock(1) on the contract. 4. Verify owner() returns address(0).
